burdens.description: Show that a supreme necessary foundation is a comparatively simple and non-arbitrary account of the initial reality.
burdens.successCriteria: State a stable no-arbitrary-limits principle, justify applying it to the initial reality, and show why the resulting supreme characterization costs no more than the naturalistic alternative.

burdens.description: Show that a supreme foundation unifies otherwise separate necessary, axiological, and mind-related features of reality.
burdens.successCriteria: Supply warranted derivations from supremacy to specific attributes and risky predictions, then explain why unification improves the total worldview rather than merely redescribing it.

burdens.description: Show that consciousness is irreducibly mental and is better expected on a mind-first foundation.
burdens.successCriteria: Defend the epistemic and metaphysical inference from first-person awareness to irreducibility, answer identity theory, and connect the result comparatively to the foundation.

burdens.description: Defend epistemic restraint about the necessary initial natural reality and resist adding minded or supreme attributes without adequate warrant.
burdens.successCriteria: Give a coherent naturalistic initial-state proposal, identify the relevant evidential limits, and explain why supremacy or mind is an added commitment rather than a limit merely removed.

burdens.description: Establish that worldview comparison must assess total commitments and consequences rather than local simplicity alone.
burdens.successCriteria: Explain how downstream commitments affect comparative simplicity and apply the standard consistently to both complete worldviews.

burdens.description: Defend a naturalistic identity account of consciousness against the introspective distinction argument.
burdens.successCriteria: State the identity view precisely, show why introspection does not discriminate it from rivals, and provide an evidence-based warrant for preferring the neural account.
